card.what: Forged stainless snap hook, 75 mm: spliced to halyards, spinnaker sheets, flag halyards and dock lines to clip onto a sail's head, a ring or a padeye
card.boats: new kit part: the J/22's jib and main halyards and spinnaker sheets carry one each; the Sunfish's halyard; dock lines at the club
card.distance: arm's reach at the mast and on the foredeck when hoisting; the camera sees it in hand
card.before: none: the kit had no snap hook (the nearest stand-in was the 5 mm D-shackle, ShackleD)

references.use: outline and proportions (square-on face view on white; turned so the long axis is vertical by mask_white_bg.py --rotate auto)
references.url: project upload from Bean, Nov 8 2026 (sheet of sailboat hardware, top left 'Snap Hook'); a catalogue-style photo: measuring only, not in the repo

references.note: 75 mm forged 316L snap hook of this style: length 75 mm, A 12 mm, B 10 mm, 67 g (also listed in 50 mm, A 8 / B 6, and 100 mm, A 16 / B 13). The listings don't say which letters are which: A read as the gate opening, B as the eye's width; both reported, not scored

sizes.name: Overall length, crown to the bottom of the eye
Length / width (face view)
sizes.source: measured on the square-on photo (score.py's aspect_full is height / width of the outline)

sizes.name: Width across the face, gate to spine

features.text: One forged teardrop body, flattened-oval sections, no seams
Turned-down nose at the top of the gate side; the gate's tip tucks under it
Wire spring gate: a narrow loop of stainless wire from the palm up to the nose
Oval eye through the palm for the line, tilted along the body
Round raised boss on the face beside the eye, with a square rivet in it
The spine (back) is the beefiest part; the nose arm thinner
Room in the bite for a 12 mm ring or a sail's head

budget.note: hero is a Nanite part; build_kit makes the light copy at a quarter of the triangles
